title: IMF Managing Director at Wall Street Journal CEO Council Meeting : CSPAN2 : December 24, 2019 7:43am-8:02am EST
text:
7:43 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            >> weeknights this week featuring booktv programs on c-span2. neil gorsuch reflects on his 30 year career and offer spots on the judiciary and u.s. constitution. justice ruth bader ginsburg recounts her time on the high court at the book festival. we will hear from the federalist's molly hemingway and judicial crisis network examining the confirmation of brett kavanaugh, watch tuesday night on c-span2 and enjoy booktv this week and every weekend on c-span2. the managing director of the international monetary fund speak at the annual ceo council meeting in washington dc.           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:44 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            >> give us a primer on the us economy talking about the international economy. kristalina georgieva is the managing director of the new chief of the imf. let's see what her prognosis is for markets outside the united states. [applause] >> happy to have you here. >> let's get right into it. we had an upbeat view of the us economy and complaints about the global economy. let's start with the us. despite everything we have seen a slowdown in us growth this year and a slump in manufacturing, decline in business investment. from your perch, what is your outlook for the us economy in the coming years?           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:45 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            >> the us is in a good place. people in this room have contributed to that, the longest in history, expansion, lowest in the last 50 years. to see that wages, and low-paid workers out facing wage growth on average driven by productivity gains, very important to recognize but you are right that there are issues, manufacturing and agriculture, what we see consumption and services being the drivers of that good growth. we see in the united states           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:46 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            like every where prolonged periods of low interest rates, looking for more leverage, and in the household -- >> you see invulnerability. >> this is something to be mindful of because we cannot make a prediction that they would be never a financial, more often than not, financial institutions that means higher risk so we have to watch it. this is a liability. we also see room to do more for the poorest americans. i was listening to the next           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:47 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            generation of policy measures. it would be good to target a boost for the economy and i would say last but not least, it can do better if there is less uncertainty in trade. we being an institution that loves to wrestle with numbers. we have trade sessions costing the world economy $700 billion by next year but more important than the number is the breakdown. only one third of this number comes from paris directly. 63% comes from uncertainty. and 4% comes from a productivity loss and our expectation is unless tensions           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:48 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            are handled we would see global value chains and more feedback on productivity so dealing with uncertainty would be really great in the us and elsewhere. >> are you seeing in 2020 continued slowdown in the us economy or stabilizing? >> our projection is 1% from next year, it is 2.4% this year so based on today's assessment we see a little slowdown, not by much. we see very vibrant consumer demand driven by what we just describe it. service - how would manufacturing be affected next year there was less trade uncertainty, we can expect a           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:49 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            good number there. >> host: as we pull back the lens and ask the same question globally of the imf in october lowered its forecast for global growth, what are you seeing in 2020? do you see a rebound or continued slowing? >> when they feel we are projecting 3.4% it is a rebound but also the outside risks, mostly it would come from particularly slow this year. being less slow or rebounding, may be doing a little better. we are recognizing a number of bright spots in the world. they are growing 5% or more.           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:50 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            >> host: where are the bright spots? >> guest: i would start -- the countries are doing well and certainties, 5% or more. it contributes to global growth 10%, as much because us contributes to global growth. we are -- a number of countries in africa that people are not paying enough attention to but looking for the right investments, the way growth is 7%, 8%, 9% to reform their business environment, the country makes senegal, and that country. we do see two vulnerabilities in the world we have not seen in our october forecast.           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:51 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            when is india slowing down more than we anticipated and very clearly people on the streets means economies are slowing down. this is happening in hong kong, chile, colombia, lebanon. whether this unrest is sustained is a downside risk to that forecast. >> host: let's go to the dragon in the room, china, second-largest economy. the global slowdown this year, china alone its double digit growth years contributed to the global economy. do you see it stabilizing or slumping more? >> global growth slowing down. we expect them to grow at 6.1%.           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:52 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            it was 6.5% but on the lower end, and we project china to grow 6%. it is partially because the natural process of shifting from high-speed to high-quality growth, to more domestic consumption of growth. if you look at the numbers on how trade tensions affect the world's economy china has more of that impact because it is more export oriented and the economy of china, on the horizon, not good news for the           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:53 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            members but china does have space to boost its economy. what they are looking at is moderate action on the monetary policy side, stimulus the this time is not going to be infrastructure projects. this is what china used to do. now they are more oriented towards africa as a measure to stimulate like what you were thinking about the us and china certainly has a lot of space to boost a certain sector by opening up the financial sector. i was in china a week ago. all the conversations from president xi to regulators were about china being determined to open financial services, the imf support to the regulatory agencies in that area.           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:54 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            >> china has a debt issue and the leaders who are reluctant to engage in stimulus because they want to curb the growth of debt. >> rather than directing assessments to pass, they -- like many in the low interest rate environment recognizing one specific area they need to concentrate on, small banks where they are vulnerable and taking actions in that direction and the price reform. what is happening is because of uncertainty which is the new normal, they are more reluctant than they were a year ago to more aggressively tackle reform.           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:55 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            what would happen about losing their jobs more rapidly. >> you mentioned india. do you think we will ever see india taking on the role china played in recent years. they look at india through the next remaining big economy that could go into a double digit growth. >> they are right to do that because of the bright spots i talked about. the answer to your question is india has that potential. south asia overall, bangladesh, india, these are questions with average age of 27 years, but advanced economies and dragged to growth and we had a useful country. they are mindful that they had           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:56 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            to be much more serious - they are at the moment looking into a compilation of measures. will they be the next china, double digit growth rates? all we can do is put a strong prayer and provide the best that continue to make them come true. >> questions from the audience on the global economy? >> you touched on africa, two things we have seen. what is corruption and the second is political volatility, the molecules in that direction. aging the population and           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:57 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            potential but doesn't seem to work. >> it is finally sinking into a good number of african leaders but i'm encouraged by what i saw in the senegal. of recognition that they are serious about corruption nevermind what else they do. they would have a hard time attracting investors. we also have to recognize if they make efforts to improve that environment but nothing happens we may be disempowering the leadership in africa so what we are starting to do at the firms is work harder at providing objective picture in           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:58 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            africa and differentiate between those that raise an important point. it is a big continent with so many countries. and in those investments on the basis of government. >> other questions over here? >> the pension plan. we heard larry kudlow talk about interest rates for a long time, $750 trillion of debt in the world, will be sitting here in a few years with $500 trillion of debt with interest rates, are they concerned about that? >> at the annual meetings this           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      7:59 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            year, low for longer, low forever. the conclusion was twofold where we spent the imf but the other is we need to appreciate low interest rates as the contributing factor but if we didn't have low interest rates, growth this year would be half a percentage point lower, 2.5%, that is not happening. when it is prolonged, what happens, financial institutions are taking excessive risk, sooner or later that risk may come to violins and in addition to this we have to recognize the underlying reason for low           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      8:00 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            interest rates, talking about markets, is sleeping beauty called productivity. and rightly so many of us are saying, and monetary policy. we have to talk about fiscal authority and structural reforms. we have to wake up sleeping beauty and get the growth coming from productivity as well. ..           
        
    
  
    
    
                            
      8:01 am    
          
        
      
          
                      
                                
                                
                  
      
          
            judges on the fourth circuit court of appeals heard oral argument in two lawsuits that claim president trump violated the emolument clause of the constitution which bars president from receiving gifts from ford or state government while in office. next the oral arguments. o yay, o yay, o yay, all persons having manner or form of business before the honorable united states court of appeals for the fourth circuit bring their attention for the court is now sitting. god save the united states and this honorable court. >> mr. mooppan. >> may it please the court. maryland and the district of columbia seek to assert an applied cause of action to enforce the emolument clause is
